text: Hi, I'm Vaibhav Jangid, co-founder of Hisab on Monad. I lead product and engineering.
And I'm Bhavya Dhoot, the other co-founder. I build the smart contracts and the backend.
Here's the problem. An exporter ships today, but gets paid sixty to ninety days later.
So their working capital sits locked in every open invoice. And banks finance collateral, not invoices.
Small tickets cost more to underwrite and reconcile than they earn.
Lenders stay away too. There is no shared record of whether past invoices were paid, and the same invoice can be pledged twice.
The result is a trade-finance gap, estimated in the trillions of dollars.
So we built Hisab on Monad. The shipping bill is tokenised, and the buyer acknowledges it with a signature.
Then a lender pool advances A U S D the day the goods ship, priced by the exporter's onchain credit tier.
In our demo, the exporter sees thirty-nine thousand, and accepts it in one click.
Try to finance the same bill twice, and the contract refuses. Double financing, blocked.
When the buyer pays, one transaction repays the pool, takes the fee, and pays the exporter.
Pay on time, and the exporter moves up a tier. Eighty percent advance becomes eighty-eight.
The original Hisab matched messy SWIFT payment messages to shipments. It only recorded entitlements.
On Monad, the money itself moves, in A U S D. Blocks take four hundred milliseconds.
And fees stay low enough for a ten-thousand-dollar invoice.
Lenders get a shared onchain credit record to price from. That is what makes the next offer cheaper.
It's live on Monad testnet today.
